verses.original: Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ἀδελφοί γινώσκουσιν γὰρ νόμον λαλῶ ὅτι ὁ νόμος κυριεύει τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ
verses.transliteration: Ē agnoeite adelphoi ginōskousin gar nomon lalō hoti ho nomos kyrieuei tou anthrōpou eph’ hoson chronon zē
verses.literal: Do you not know brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law) that the law has authority over a man only as long as . . . he lives
verses.literalPt: Porventura, ignorais, irmãos pois falo aos que conhecem a lei, que ela tem domínio sobre o homem durante todo o tempo que ele vive?

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός
verses.transliteration: hē gar hypandros gynē tō zōnti andri dedetai nomō ean de apothanē ho anēr katērgētai apo tou nomou tou andros
verses.literal: For instance . . . a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives But if her husband dies she is released from the law of marriage
verses.literalPt: A mulher casada está ligada pela lei a seu marido, enquanto ele vive; mas, se o marido morrer, desligada fica da lei do marido.

verses.original: ἄρα οὖν ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν μοιχαλίδα γενομένην ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ
verses.transliteration: ara oun zōntos tou andros moichalis chrēmatisei ean genētai andri heterō ean de apothanē ho anēr eleuthera estin apo tou nomou tou mē einai autēn moichalida genomenēn andri heterō
verses.literal: So then if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive she is called an adulteress but if her husband dies she is free from that law and is not an adulteress if she marries another man
verses.literalPt: Assim, pois, enquanto o marido vive, se ela for de outro homem, será chamada adúltera; mas, se morrer o marido, livre está da lei, de maneira que não é adúltera, se for de outro homem.

verses.original: Ὥστε ἀδελφοί μου καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐθανατώθητε τῷ νόμῳ διὰ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι ὑμᾶς ἑτέρῳ τῷ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθέντι ἵνα καρποφορήσωμεν τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: Hōste adelphoi mou kai hymeis ethanatōthēte tō nomō dia tou sōmatos tou Christou eis to genesthai hymas heterō tō ek nekrōn egerthenti hina karpophorēsōmen tō Theō
verses.literal: Therefore my brothers you also died to the law through the body of Christ that you might belong to another to Him who was raised from the dead in order that we might bear fruit to God
verses.literalPt: De modo que, meus irmãos, também vós fostes mortos à Lei, pelo corpo de Cristo, para pertencerdes a outro, àquele que foi ressuscitado dentre os mortos, a fim de que déssemos fruto a Deus.

verses.original: ὅτε γὰρ ἦμεν ἐν τῇ σαρκί τὰ παθήματα τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν τὰ διὰ τοῦ νόμου ἐνηργεῖτο ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ καρποφορῆσαι τῷ θανάτῳ
verses.transliteration: hote gar ēmen en tē sarki ta pathēmata tōn hamartiōn ta dia tou nomou enērgeito en tois melesin hēmōn eis to karpophorēsai tō thanatō
verses.literal: For when we lived according to the flesh the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies bearing fruit for death
verses.literalPt: Pois, quando estávamos na carne, as paixões dos pecados que havia pela Lei operaram em nossos membros, a fim de darem fruto à morte;

verses.original: νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος
verses.transliteration: nyni de katērgēthēmen apo tou nomou apothanontes en hō kateichometha hōste douleuein hēmas en kainotēti pneumatos kai ou palaiotēti grammatos
verses.literal: But now having died to what bound us we have been released from the law so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit and not in the old way of the written code
verses.literalPt: mas, agora, desligados estamos da Lei, por termos morrido para aquilo em que estávamos presos, de sorte que sirvamos em novidade de espírito e não na velhice da letra.

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν ὁ νόμος ἁμαρτία μὴ γένοιτο ἀλλὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔγνων εἰ μὴ διὰ νόμου τήν τε γὰρ ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν εἰ μὴ ὁ νόμος ἔλεγεν Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις
verses.transliteration: Ti oun eroumen ho nomos hamartia mē genoito alla tēn hamartian ouk egnōn ei mē dia nomou tēn te gar epithymian ouk ēdein ei mē ho nomos elegen Ouk epithymēseis
verses.literal: What then shall we say Is the law sin Certainly not Indeed I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said Do not covet
verses.literalPt: Que diremos, pois? É a Lei pecado? De modo nenhum! Mas eu não teria conhecido o pecado, senão pela Lei; pois eu não teria conhecido a cobiça, se a Lei não dissera: Não cobiçarás.

verses.original: ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς κατειργάσατο ἐν ἐμοὶ πᾶσαν ἐπιθυμίαν χωρὶς γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία νεκρά
verses.transliteration: aphormēn de labousa hē hamartia dia tēs entolēs kateirgasato en emoi pasan epithymian chōris gar nomou hamartia nekra
verses.literal: But sin seizing its opportunity through the commandment produced in me every kind of covetous desire For apart from the law sin is dead
verses.literalPt: Mas o pecado, achando ocasião, operou em mim, pelo mandamento, toda a cobiça; porque, sem a Lei, o pecado está morto.

verses.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ ἔζων χωρὶς νόμου ποτέ ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀνέζησεν ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπέθανον
verses.transliteration: Egō de ezōn chōris nomou pote elthousēs de tēs entolēs hē hamartia anezēsen egō de apethanon
verses.literal: Once I was alive apart from the law but when the commandment came sin sprang to life and I died
verses.literalPt: Em outro tempo, eu vivia sem a Lei, mas, quando veio o mandamento, reviveu o pecado, e eu morri.

verses.original: καὶ εὑρέθη μοι ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ εἰς ζωὴν αὕτη εἰς θάνατον
verses.transliteration: kai heurethē moi hē entolē hē eis zōēn hautē eis thanaton
verses.literal: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death
verses.literalPt: O mandamento que era para vida, esse achei que era para morte;

verses.original: ἡ γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφορμὴν λαβοῦσα διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με καὶ δι’ αὐτῆς ἀπέκτεινεν
verses.transliteration: hē gar hamartia aphormēn labousa dia tēs entolēs exēpatēsen me kai di’ autēs apekteinen
verses.literal: For sin seizing its opportunity through the commandment deceived me and through the commandment put me to death
verses.literalPt: porque o pecado, achando ocasião, me enganou pelo mandamento e por ele me matou.

verses.original: Ὥστε ὁ μὲν νόμος ἅγιος καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθή
verses.transliteration: Hōste ho men nomos hagios kai hē entolē hagia kai dikaia kai agathē
verses.literal: So then the law is holy and the commandment is holy righteous and good
verses.literalPt: De modo que a Lei é santa, e o mandamento é santo, justo e bom.

verses.original: Τὸ οὖν ἀγαθὸν ἐμοὶ ἐγένετο θάνατος μὴ γένοιτο ἀλλὰ ἡ ἁμαρτία ἵνα φανῇ ἁμαρτία διὰ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ μοι κατεργαζομένη θάνατον ἵνα γένηται καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς
verses.transliteration: To oun agathon emoi egeneto thanatos mē genoito alla hē hamartia hina phanē hamartia dia tou agathou moi katergazomenē thanaton hina genētai kath’ hyperbolēn hamartōlos hē hamartia dia tēs entolēs
verses.literal: Did that which is good then become death to me Certainly not But in order that sin might be exposed as sin it produced death in me through what was good so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful
verses.literalPt: Logo, o que é bom tornou-se morte para mim? De modo nenhum! Mas sim o pecado, para se mostrar pecado, operando em mim a morte por meio do que é bom, a fim de que, pelo mandamento, o pecado se fizesse excessivamente mau.

verses.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ὁ νόμος πνευματικός ἐστιν ἐγὼ δὲ σάρκινός εἰμι πεπραμένος ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν
verses.transliteration: Oidamen gar hoti ho nomos pneumatikos estin egō de sarkinos eimi pepramenos hypo tēn hamartian
verses.literal: We know that the law is spiritual but I am unspiritual sold as a slave to sin
verses.literalPt: Sabemos que a Lei é espiritual; mas eu sou de carne, vendido para estar sujeito ao pecado.

verses.original: ὃ γὰρ κατεργάζομαι οὐ γινώσκω οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω τοῦτο πράσσω ἀλλ’ ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο ποιῶ
verses.transliteration: ho gar katergazomai ou ginōskō ou gar ho thelō touto prassō all’ ho misō touto poiō
verses.literal: I do not understand what I do For what I want to do I do not do But what I hate I do
verses.literalPt: Pois o que faço não entendo: não pratico o que quero, mas faço o que aborreço.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ σύμφημι τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι καλός
verses.transliteration: ei de ho ou thelō touto poiō symphēmi tō nomō hoti kalos
verses.literal: And if I do what I do not want to do I admit that the law is good
verses.literalPt: Mas, se faço aquilo que não quero, admito que a Lei é boa.

verses.original: νυνὶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία
verses.transliteration: nyni de ouketi egō katergazomai auto alla hē oikousa en emoi hamartia
verses.literal: In that case it is no longer I who do it but it is sin living in me that does it
verses.literalPt: Porém, agora, não sou eu mais o que faço isso, mas o pecado que em mim habita.

verses.original: Οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἐμοί τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου ἀγαθόν τὸ γὰρ θέλειν παράκειταί μοι τὸ δὲ κατεργάζεσθαι τὸ καλὸν οὔ
verses.transliteration: Oida gar hoti ouk oikei en emoi tout’ estin en tē sarki mou agathon to gar thelein parakeitai moi to de katergazesthai to kalon ou
verses.literal: I know that nothing good lives in me that is in my flesh for I have the desire to do what is good but I cannot carry it out
verses.literalPt: Eu sei que em mim, isto é, na minha carne, não habita o bem; o querer o bem está comigo, mas o efetuá-lo não está.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω ποιῶ ἀγαθόν ἀλλὰ ὃ οὐ θέλω κακὸν τοῦτο πράσσω
verses.transliteration: ou gar ho thelō poiō agathon alla ho ou thelō kakon touto prassō
verses.literal: For I do not do the good I want to do Instead I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do
verses.literalPt: Pois não faço o bem que quero; mas o mal que não quero, este pratico.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω ἐγὼ τοῦτο ποιῶ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία
verses.transliteration: ei de ho ou thelō egō touto poiō ouketi egō katergazomai auto alla hē oikousa en emoi hamartia
verses.literal: And if I do what I do not want it is no longer I who do it but it is sin living in me that does it
verses.literalPt: Mas, se eu faço aquilo que não quero, já não sou eu o que faço, mas sim o pecado que em mim habita.

verses.original: Εὑρίσκω ἄρα τὸν νόμον τῷ θέλοντι ἐμοὶ ποιεῖν τὸ καλὸν ὅτι ἐμοὶ τὸ κακὸν παράκειται
verses.transliteration: Heuriskō ara ton nomon tō thelonti emoi poiein to kalon hoti emoi to kakon parakeitai
verses.literal: So this is the principle I have discovered When I want to do good - evil is right there with me
verses.literalPt: Portanto, querendo eu fazer o bem, acho a lei de que está comigo o mal.

verses.original: συνήδομαι γὰρ τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: synēdomai gar tō nomō tou Theou kata ton esō anthrōpon
verses.literal: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law
verses.literalPt: Pois eu me deleito na Lei de Deus, no homem interior;

verses.original: βλέπω δὲ ἕτερον νόμον ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου ἀντιστρατευόμενον τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ νοός μου καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντά με ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τῷ ὄντι ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου
verses.transliteration: blepō de heteron nomon en tois melesin mou antistrateuomenon tō nomō tou noos mou kai aichmalōtizonta me en tō nomō tēs hamartias tō onti en tois melesin mou
verses.literal: But I see another law at work in my body warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me
verses.literalPt: mas vejo uma lei diferente nos meus membros, guerreando a lei do meu espírito e fazendo-me preso na lei do pecado, a qual está nos meus membros.

verses.original: Ταλαίπωρος ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος τίς με ῥύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ θανάτου τούτου
verses.transliteration: Talaipōros egō anthrōpos tis me rhysetai ek tou sōmatos tou thanatou toutou
verses.literal: What a wretched man I am Who will rescue me from this body of death
verses.literalPt: Infeliz homem eu! Quem me livrará do corpo desta morte?

verses.original: χάρις δὲ τῷ Θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἄρα οὖν αὐτὸς ἐγὼ τῷ μὲν νοῒ δουλεύω νόμῳ Θεοῦ τῇ δὲ σαρκὶ νόμῳ ἁμαρτίας
verses.transliteration: charis de tō Theō dia Iēsou Christou tou Kyriou hēmōn Ara oun autos egō tō men noi douleuō nomō Theou tē de sarki nomō hamartias
verses.literal: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord So then with my mind I serve the law of God but with my flesh I serve the law of sin
verses.literalPt: Graças a Deus por Jesus Cristo, nosso Senhor. Assim, pois, eu mesmo, com o espírito, sirvo à lei de Deus, mas com a carne sirvo à lei do pecado.
